text:
anya: Heads-up — Humboldt-70B goes live next Tue (canary then global). asking for a quick capacity projection + what we should pre-provision in us-east1/us-west2/eu-west1.

mike: Thanks. rough traffic shape from the beta tests: bursty spikes during onboarding with median 220 rps, 95th 1.1k rps, avg seq ~220 tokens. We're expecting a PLG-triggered ramp first 48h.

sanjay: Quick question — are you expecting streaming responses or single-shot? that changes batching behavior a lot.

anya: Streaming by default for chat flows, single-shot for some sync endpoints. overall mix ~65% streaming.

mike: ok. quick back-of-envelope: assume 1.1k rps * 220 tokens = 242k tokens/sec peak. With our current serving profile (Humboldt 70B quantized, 16-way KV shards) one A100-equivalent can sustain ~28k tokens/sec under expected lat SLOs. So peak token load -> ~9 A100 equiv. add 30% headroom + autoscale lag => recommend pre-warm 12 GPUs in each primary region during launch window.

jess: 12 GPUs each region seems heavy. what's the expected GPU-hours and cost delta?

mike: math in case it helps:```
peak_tokens_sec = 242000
per_gpu_tokens_sec = 28000
required_gpus = ceil(peak_tokens_sec / per_gpu_tokens_sec) = 9
prewarm = round(required_gpus * 1.33) = 12
```
If we prewarm 12 GPUs in us-east1 + 12 in us-west2 + 6 in eu-west1 for 48 hours: GPU-hours = (12+12+6) * 48 = 1440 GPU-hours. At our internal cost ~ $1.8 / GPU-hour -> ~ $2.6k. If sustained longer, scale proportionally.

sanjay: Note: network egress and KV-cache pressure will increase. During the beta we saw 15% higher RPC retries on us-west2 under sustained bursts — need tighter connection pool limits.

anya: Good call. can we set canary routing to 10% traffic for first 2 hours, then 30% for next 4 hours, 60% next 12, 100% if healthy? Also want auto-fallback to a smaller 13B variant if latency > 600ms for 1m.

mike: We can implement that rollout policy in traffic-router. I'll add prewarm job to allocate nodes 90m before canary. For fallback, we need compatible model variant available in the same region; confirm with model onbarding.

jess: From product: confirm audit logs for every fallback and per-request model id in tracing so we can debug quality regressions.

ops-bot: deploybot: canary-config updated by mike at 1902123503 — routing rules: 10%->30%->60%->100% windows and fallback policy set to Humboldt-13B variant.

mike: Also flagging a quota bump request for dedicated pools: current soft quotas per region will block >8 GPUs/node pools. I'll open a ticket with cloud ops to allow up to 24 GPUs prewarm per region for the launch.

sanjay: On-call checklist:
- verify KV cache warm-up script runs after prewarm nodes come up (job id: kv-warm-1902)
- increase client connection pool timeout from 30s -> 45s for initial launch window
- watch RPC retry rate and tail-latency dashboards (SLO: p99 < 800ms)

anya: Can someone post a short runbook snippet here for support to follow during the first 6 hours? Keep it simple: what to do if tail latency crosses 1s, or token ops drop.

mike: Runbook snippet:```
If p99 latency > 1s for > 3m:
  1) Shift 20% traffic to Humboldt-13B variant (traffic-router)
  2) Pause canary ramp and notify #eng-sre and #product
  3) Check KV cache warm-up job and rpc-retry graph
  4) If CPU on gateway >85% add 2 additional gateways from spare pool
If token throughput drops >30% uncorrelated with upstream errors:
  1) Check inter-region packet loss (net-dash)
  2) Validate model shard health on nodes (shard-ctl status)
```

jess: will put that into a short doc and link to support.

anya: final ask — can we get a conservative 72h GPU-hours estimate (for budgeting) and a worst-case cost ceiling for finance?

mike: Conservative 72h estimate: prewarm plan -> (12+12+6)=30 GPUs * 72h = 2160 GPU-hours. Add 20% buffer for scale-ups = 2592 GPU-hours. At $1.8 / GPU-hour -> ~$4.7k. Worst-case if sustained high for 7 days without rollback: 30 * 168 = 5040 GPU-hours -> ~$9.1k. I'll post numbers to the finance ticket.

sanjay: I'll monitor the network and on-call page during the window and escalate if we see region-specific congestion.

anya: thanks all — appreciate quick turnaround. tagging @mike and @sanjay for follow-ups.
